messages:
Eli: heads up — after the RBAC roles/bindings refactor merged in PR #3421 we noticed a weird KMS access path when projects were moved into the new shared-workspace namespace. quick summary: an engineer moved proj-42 into shared-workspace and a service in org-b was briefly able to request decrypt operations on proj-42's KMS key.

Mira: whoa. do we have audit logs showing the calls? KMS logs or platform audit?

security-bot: alert triggered: KMS key policy anomaly detected for key=k-key-prod-xyz, requester=svc-ingest@org-b, action=Decrypt, time=2026-11-03T15:12:03Z. link: https://console.redwood/kms/logs/abc123

Sam: timeline: PR #3421 changed the binding evaluation order so resource -> workspace mapping was computed lazily. when a project is moved we briefly returned an empty org claim during policy eval which let a fallback binding match (read-only) that had a broader principal. looks like an ordering/regression.

Jordan: can you paste the offending snippet?

Sam: sure — reproduced locally:

```json
{
  "binding": {
    "role": "projects/kms.decrypt",
    "members": ["role:svc-ingest"]
  },
  "condition": {
    "expression": "resource.org == null || resource.workspace == 'shared-workspace'"
  }
}
```

Sam: basically the condition allowed a match when resource.org was null during the brief window after move. old evaluator guaranteed resource.org resolution before condition eval. new lazy path did not.

Mira: but why did KMS allow a decrypt? KMS keys also have key policies — were those bypassed?

Eli: quick postmortem: key policy required project-owner approval, but our cross-service trust model had a delegated check that looked at the platform RBAC result and accepted it. since RBAC returned match, the delegated check passed. KMS-managed policy still logged the call but linked to the platform principal.

Jordan: severity? did anyone read secrets? looks like decrypt was used for a non-sensitive bootstrap token only. no PII. tentative sev2.

security-bot: incident logged: INC-2026-304. affected: 1 decrypt on k-key-prod-xyz (bootstrap token), no other key ops.

Mira: mitigation steps done?

Sam: hotfix deployed 1789001200: revert PR #3421 ordering change and reapply evaluation that resolves resource.org before matching fallback bindings. rolled back within ~6 minutes of detection.

Ops-bot: deployment note: hotfix deployed to prod via canary -> all nodes green. CI run: e2e-rbac-tests (added new case) passed.

Eli: additional fixes:
- add deterministic mapping recompute in the project-move flow so resource.org is set synchronously before any policy evaluation path runs
- add guard in binding evaluator: require explicit org claim for workspace-scoped fallback bindings
- patch the delegated KMS check to re-validate key policy explicitly (defense in depth)

Sam: created tickets: PLAT-4973 (recompute-on-move), PLAT-4974 (binding-evaluator-guard), SECG-212 (kms-delegation-hardening). assigned owners: Sam, Mira, Jordan respectively.

Mira: audit improvements — we should link platform RBAC decision id to KMS audit entries so we can trace cross-system auths. filed AUD-89.

Jordan: tests we added:
- unit: evaluator where resource.org is null -> must not match workspace fallback
- e2e: move project -> immediate policy check -> no transient null orgs
- fuzz: 1000 random move permutations to ensure no race

Eli: long-term: do we want an invariant that resource.* metadata must be eventual-consistent-before-any-auth? or enforce synchronous set during control-plane ops?

Mira: prefer synchronous for move operations (rare but high-impact). for bulk ops we can schedule background recompute but block any auth checks until recompute snapshot reaches the requestor.

Sam: also adding an alert: any KMS decrypt where platform-rbac.decision == 'ALLOW' but resource.org != requester.org -> auto-raise sec-signal.

Jordan: to follow up: 1) postmortem draft (wg: sec+platform) 2) ship PLAT tickets 3) update runbook for project moves 4) telemetry dashboard for cross-org key ops.

Eli: who will own postmortem?

Mira: I can own draft. target: publish within 72h.

Sam: I'll PR the quick evaluator guard now, mark as hotfix candidate if needed.

Eli: thanks. quick note for oncall: if you see KMS anomaly alert with decision id present, escalate to eng-security immediately.

Jordan: adding follow-up meeting: 30m in #calendar 2026-11-04 09:00 PT. invite: Eli, Mira, Sam, Jordan, infra leads.

security-bot: reminders: attach logs to INC-2026-304 and add SECG-212 link.

Eli: closing loop — rolling forward the hotfix and the rebuild is the plan. we'll post the postmortem and update the move/runbook. thanks team :thumbsup:
